initial_product_spec.summary: Repair TRACE-12, TRACE-13, TRACE-20, TRACE-22, TRACE-02, TRACE-03, and TRACE-21 so isolated workflow execution has honest gate ownership, faithful failure comparison, snapshot/candidate isolation, actor-aware scope enforcement, observable Copilot progress and liveness, and executable read-only verification. Deliver seven independent outcomes through a maximally useful two-cohort DAG, within the operator's three-cohort ceiling.

user_stories.description: As a source worker, I can submit completed work with explicitly pending harness checks, so authoritative results can settle the attempt once.
As a reviewer of baselined checks, I can distinguish unchanged failures from new or worsened failure substance despite volatile execution output.
As an operator of isolated worktrees, I can continue a run on its valid snapshots and explicitly selected candidate executable while another session changes the shared controller.
As an isolated verifier or ship worker, I receive a scope result based on my process's authority and mutations while actual unauthorized writes remain detectable.
As a supervisor, I can observe a silent but live Copilot worker without a false stall and detect its actual termination or deterministic wrapper fault.
As a supervisor, I can read sanitized Copilot launch, session, and progress evidence while its execution remains open.

As a read-only QA worker or verifier, I receive prepared runtime outputs, independently collected execution observations, and a harness validation route needed for an honest verdict without a shell grant.

constraints: C-01: Repair exactly the seven selected findings; other intake findings remain context unless tightly coupled correctness requires a change.

C-04: Preserve assertion substance, stable failure identity, genuine multiplicity, command identity, exit code, signal, and timeout differences when normalizing execution noise.

C-05: Valid recorded snapshots remain authoritative. Corrupt required snapshots and invalid new-run configuration still fail. Do not mutate active_config, persistent model settings, or recorded snapshots to compensate for drift.
C-06: Preserve write policies and prevention/detection of real unauthorized writes. Shared checkout deltas alone do not identify an actor; absent enforcement or custody must be explicit.
C-07: Preserve the fixed 60-second watch cadence, attach/recovery behavior, and the distinction between running, completed, and successful results.
C-08: Streaming preserves synchronous delegation mutex ownership, prompt-on-stdin, credential isolation, model checks, resume/fallback semantics, bounded evidence, and cleanup.
C-09: Read-only stages receive no shell tool. Declared harness collection must precede grading of required execution observations; missing or stale evidence cannot become a pass.

engineering_plan.approach: Use existing workflow boundaries and no new packages. Cohort 1 repairs criterion ownership, failure normalization, snapshot/candidate isolation, and Copilot transport in separate worktrees. Cohort 2 independently consumes the integrated transport for custody and watch, and the integrated criterion/scaffold contract for mandatory read-only execution evidence. Keep the adapter synchronous using a Node relay; keep gate results separate from original self-claims; retain conservative diagnostic and custody fallbacks; expose bounded structured collection rather than granting read-only workers a shell. Existing light verification already includes the ship release gate, so no level change is recommended.

components.approach: Add pending_harness only for resolved invocation-owned harness shell checks. Align schema, normalization, preflight, scaffold, and submit eligibility. Retain pre-gate validation of worker-owned claims and declared non-success short-circuiting. Resolve eligible pending entries from one authoritative deterministic run before success, retaining the original worker claims. Treat missing results and unauthorized skips as nonpassing; preserve explicit gate-disable authority and entry reuse.
interfaces: CriterionResultValue and stage-output schema accept pending_harness under invocation ownership, not as a general judgment result.
validateStageOutput and validateOutputForSubmission agree on eligibility.
submitOutput and effectiveOutcome require authoritative resolution while preserving self-evaluation evidence.
scaffoldStageOutput and isUntouchedScaffold still reject unfinished outputs.
components.migration: Continue accepting existing valid pass/fail outputs. Do not reinterpret unevaluated as pending or rewrite old submissions/snapshots.

components.approach: Extract recognized runner failure records with stable case identity, assertion/error substance, and true occurrence counts. Remove only proven execution metadata in known positions. Keep raw-result readers, multiset delta output, conservative unsupported-output diagnostics, and independent command/status failures. Replay fixtures directly instead of rerunning long suites.
interfaces: commandFailureDiagnostics and failureDiagnostics produce stable identities without discarding expected/actual values.
failureStatuses preserves command, exit, signal, and timeout meaning.
compareRepositoryCheckToBaseline retains its public comparison shape.
components.migration: Existing saved raw results remain inputs. Do not rewrite historical baselines; distinguish synthetic fixtures from recovered provenance-bearing transcripts.

components.approach: Load a valid recorded snapshot before advisory inspection. Catch only known live-config/projection compatibility errors in the advisory branch and emit a specific visible advisory. Exercise and document the existing explicit PANCREATOR_EXEC_ROOT boundary so a healthy candidate build administers installation state despite controller compile failure. Preserve root identity and override cleanup.
interfaces: loadRunPipelineConfig remains strict about required recorded snapshots.
runPipelineConfigAdvisories reports live incompatibility without replacing the recorded configuration.
bin/pan selects candidate executable code while PANCREATOR_ROOT, cwd, state indices, and lifecycle arguments stay bound to the installation.
components.migration: Legacy runs needing live config still fail for invalid live config. No settings translation, active_config edit, automatic build fallback, or stale-build substitution.

components.approach: Keep the synchronous adapter and delegation mutex. Add a Node relay with asynchronous CLI spawn, JSONL framing, streaming redaction, heartbeat, and child cleanup. The relay receives non-secret launch data and the prompt via stdin, credentials through environment only, writes sanitized live evidence before exit, and returns the final normalized result. Reuse the existing OpenAI adapter's child-process pattern.
interfaces: DelegationLiveRecord version 1 binds run, invocation, role, attempt, launch time, relay and worker PID/start identities, wrapper link, optional observed session, heartbeat, event sequence, and terminal exit/error.
DelegationLiveEvent records stream, receipt sequence, timestamps, event kind, and sanitized bounded content. Preserve ordering within each stream; do not invent cross-stream provider ordering.
delegationLivePaths and loadDelegationLiveRecord validate invocation-bound paths and record versions.
Heartbeat is independent of output, defaults to 30 seconds, and never exceeds 60 seconds.
Final result audit stays separate and authoritative; a result event does not imply process exit.

Relay stdout carries only the final machine envelope. Sanitized live progress reaches inherited stderr/wrapper logs and the event file before exit; accumulated sanitized CLI captures return inside the envelope for audit without parent replay.
components.migration: Keep final execution audit/result compatibility, resume/fallback, model mismatch, and prompt-on-stdin. Old records without live metadata remain readable and do not imply liveness.

components.approach: Consume the live identity and extend it with actual stageWriteRoots, enforcement mode/reason, and custody observations. Reuse resolveWriteSandbox and realpath handling rather than treating CLI read/add-dir roots as write permission. Classify own, foreign, and unverified changes using evidence; preserve strict workspace/release policy checks.
interfaces: ExternalExecutorToolPolicy records read roots separately from write authority and actual enforcement capability.
harnessRootWrites and evaluateDeterministicCriteria use process custody instead of assuming every controller delta belongs to this worker.
Own denied/unauthorized attempts remain failures; proven external edits are observations; uncertain possible own writes produce an explicit unverified result with remedy.
components.migration: Do not silently trust old records without enforcement/custody. Unsupported platforms retain an explicit conservative evidence path, never a claimed enforced boundary.

components.approach: Consult invocation-bound live process/wrapper evidence when the agent index has no activity, including an unregistered platform handle. Fresh heartbeat and matching live process suppress only quiet fallback. Preserve deterministic same-call faults, terminal audit precedence, cadence, attach behavior, and active-worker submission refusal.
interfaces: executorProcessActivity consumes live and final records using process start identity.
watchedAgentActivity and observeInvocation give available process evidence precedence over a missing index record.
quietStallApplies, deterministicStallCause, workerActivityRefusal, and assertWorkerNotStillActive agree on activity and terminal evidence.
components.migration: Retain unregistered handling for genuinely unknown agent ids, final-record fallback for old delegations, and explicit unverified state for absent/mismatched identity.

components.approach: Idempotently prepare runtime output scaffolds before read-only delegation. Add a bounded harness collector at existing preparation/evidence-dispatch boundaries; execute ratified case operations and declared source-authorized reproductions before their consuming QA/verifier grades them. Keep shell tools absent and final output validation harness-owned. Use manifests and raw observations, not implementer self-evaluation, as the independent grading input.
interfaces: Version-1 VerificationExecutionOperation declares id, criterion or finding, argv, workspace-relative cwd, timeout_ms, write_roots, and evidence_paths; validate all fields and reject free-text shell execution.

data.test_plan[].execution.operations holds ratified live-case operations; data.verification_execution_operations holds declared source-authorized reproduction handoffs. Declarations cannot expand collector write policy.
VerificationExecutionEvidence binds run/invocation/attempt/operation, exact definition, source fingerprint, actual command/time/exit/signal, sanitized raw captures, provenance, and completeness.

Evidence roles select missing declared operations via <evidence-report>.execution-request.json; final verifiers use data.verification_execution_requests. Requests contain ids and reasons, never new executable authority.

Collect newly requested authorized observations and rerun only their evidence consumer, archiving earlier reports. Reuse unchanged operation-definition/source-fingerprint results; a file's mere presence is not completeness.

A final verifier lacking required evidence uses the existing blocked shape with blocking_reason and missing_evidence_paths, without a product verdict. Unknown operations require authorized recovery before the next visit.
Configured repository profile verdicts reuse gate evidence. Browser-required observations still require genuine policy-compliant browser evidence or an explicit environment gap.
components.migration: Old plans with no required execution remain valid. Mandatory legacy free-text cases without structured authorized operations produce a specific evidence gap; do not evaluate their prose as shell or rewrite approved plans.

risks: Overnormalization can hide assertion regressions; retain literal expected/actual hashes and unknown error substance and assert exact delta identities.
Incremental sanitization can leak boundary-split secrets; sanitize before every sink and test stderr, malformed JSONL, split UTF-8, and truncation.
Liveness can be counterfeited by PID reuse, stale attempts, or early result events; bind process start identity and require final exit evidence.
OS enforcement can be unavailable; record capability honestly and keep incomplete custody explicitly unverified rather than ignoring shared mutations.
Collection can become an unauthorized command channel unless operation definitions, requests, roots, timeouts, and source fingerprints are validated separately.
Historical comparison replay may remain unavailable. Synthetic rule fixtures cannot prove equivalence of the original assertions.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An otherwise valid source-worker success with pending harness shell checks runs the required gates once, records their actual outcomes, and settles without another source-worker invocation; selected test evidence is never promoted to a profile pass.

verification.method: tests/integration/pending-harness-criteria.test.ts submits fixture full and merge-patch outputs with counted harness gates and inspects preserved worker claims plus resolved deterministic records.
verification.expected: Exactly one required gate execution per authoritative attempt; honest original pending claims remain auditable; passing gates settle success without a second source-worker call and failing gates settle failure.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Pending judgments/state/unknown criteria, unresolved required gates, and unauthorized skipped or untouched scaffold results cannot yield success; existing failed, blocked, disabled-gate, entry-reuse, and idempotent submission routes retain truthful results and execution counts.

verification.method: tests/unit/validators-stage-output.test.ts, tests/unit/requirements-scaffold.test.ts, and tests/integration/pending-harness-criteria.test.ts exercise ownership, missing evidence, disabled authority, non-success, reused entry checks, and duplicate submission.
verification.expected: Invalid/unresolved pending entries and incomplete scaffolds are rejected. Explicitly disabled or reused checks retain their provenance. Non-success short-circuits and repeated submissions do not introduce extra gate executions or fabricated passes.

acceptance_criteria.statement: Replayed failure records with identical assertion substance and occurrence counts produce zero new or fixed identities when only progress, counters, selection, temporary heads, or generated report metadata differ; historical evidence is labeled by provenance and never certified from names alone.

verification.method: tests/regression/repository-check-delta.test.ts replays provenance-bearing or explicitly synthetic paired records directly through the comparator and inspects exact diagnostic identities/counts.
verification.expected: Noise-only variants have empty new/fixed identity lists and unchanged substantive carried counts. Original-transcript replay is claimed only when the original assertion inputs were actually recovered.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A new case, changed assertion including a literal expected/actual hash, increased genuine failure multiplicity, changed command/status/signal/timeout, or unknown error output remains a detectable new or worsened diagnostic; existing baseline readers and delta consumers retain their result shape.

verification.method: tests/unit/repository-check-baseline.test.ts and tests/regression/repository-check-delta.test.ts mutate one substantive dimension at a time, including unsupported tool output and repeated failure renderings versus genuine occurrences.
verification.expected: Every actual new/worsened failure is identified with the correct multiplicity/status; duplicate display and execution noise do not inflate counts; legacy saved raw inputs and public delta fields remain usable.

acceptance_criteria.statement: A run with a valid recorded pipeline snapshot continues through lifecycle preparation and submission when live configuration/advisory projection is incompatible, emits a specific advisory, and preserves settings/snapshots; corrupt required snapshots and invalid new-run configuration still fail explicitly.

verification.method: tests/integration/lifecycle-snapshot-isolation.test.ts creates isolated run/config fixtures, changes only live configuration/projection, and exercises recorded and legacy/new-run branches.
verification.expected: Valid snapshots remain authoritative with a named advisory for live incompatibility. Required corrupt/missing snapshots, unexpected I/O, and invalid live configuration genuinely required by a new/legacy run remain errors. Persistent configuration and snapshots are byte-identical.

acceptance_criteria.statement: An explicitly selected healthy candidate executes lifecycle/worktree administration against the same installation state despite an intentionally unbuildable shared controller; state roots, argument resolution, executable provenance, override cleanup, and invalid-root errors remain correct.

verification.method: tests/integration/cli-build-wrappers-run-built.test.ts creates healthy candidate and broken-controller fixtures, selects PANCREATOR_EXEC_ROOT, and records executed code provenance, working directory, state paths, descendant environment, and invalid-root diagnostics.
verification.expected: Only the selected candidate supplies executable/build code. Lifecycle/worktree operations use the original installation indices and roots; unrelated children do not inherit the override. Invalid candidates fail explicitly rather than selecting a different build.

acceptance_criteria.statement: With proven process custody and unchanged isolated workspace authority, an unrelated session's dirty edits and clean commits in the controller remain external observations and do not fail isolated verifier or ship scope checks.

verification.expected: Foreign paths retain their evidence and are not attributed as worker violations. Both dirty controller edits and unrelated clean commits allow an otherwise valid isolated worker's scope result to pass.

# TRACE workflow friction repairs

## Request and authority

The operator requested repairs for TRACE-12, TRACE-13, TRACE-20, TRACE-22,
TRACE-02, TRACE-03, and TRACE-21, with a maximally parallel execution DAG
containing at most three cohorts. The selected workspace is
`worktrees/operator/trace-friction-t1`.

The request is recorded in
`runtime/logs/workflows/63264_Oct-15-0547_trace-fricti/operator/request.md`.
The complete repair context is
`runtime/inbox/queue/63265_Oct-14-0900_trace-copilo-run-friction.md`, especially
the seven selected finding sections. Its other findings explain the incident;
they do not expand this authorization.

This parent contains the complete product and integration contract. Each
referenced child controls its own implementation scope. A child wins within
that scope; this parent wins for system-wide context and cross-chunk interfaces.
Plan approval ratifies this hierarchy. It does not authorize a gate waiver,
an executor substitution, a configuration change, or publication.

## Product specification

### Summary

Remove seven documented obstacles to honest, isolated workflow execution.
Workers must be able to hand harness-owned checks to the harness, baseline
comparisons must distinguish failure substance from execution noise, lifecycle
operations must honor valid recorded snapshots, and scope checks must establish
custody rather than charge every shared-controller edit to every worker.
Copilot execution must expose sanitized progress and process identity before
exit. Watch must use that evidence when no agent-index entry exists. Read-only
verification must receive independently collected execution evidence and
prepared runtime artifacts through an authorized harness path.

### User stories

- US-01: As a source worker, I can submit completed work with explicitly pending
  harness checks, so their authoritative results can settle the attempt once.
  Origin: TRACE-12.
- US-02: As a reviewer of baselined checks, I can distinguish unchanged failures
  from new or worsened failure substance, despite volatile output. Origin:
  TRACE-13.
- US-03: As an operator of isolated worktrees, I can continue a run on its valid
  snapshots and candidate executable while another session edits the shared
  controller. Origin: TRACE-20.
- US-04: As an isolated verifier or ship worker, I receive a scope result based
  on my process's authority and mutations, while real unauthorized writes remain
  detectable. Origin: TRACE-22.
- US-05: As a supervisor, I can observe a silent but live Copilot worker without
  a false stall, and detect its actual termination or wrapper fault. Origin:
  TRACE-02.
- US-06: As a supervisor, I can read sanitized Copilot session and progress
  evidence while execution is still open. Origin: TRACE-03.
- US-07: As a read-only QA worker or verifier, I receive the runtime scaffold,
  mandatory execution observations, and validation route needed for an honest
  verdict without a general shell grant. Origin: TRACE-21.

### Constraints

- C-01: Repair exactly the seven selected findings; other intake findings remain
  context unless a change is necessary to preserve these repairs' correctness.
- C-02: Use the greatest useful parallelism supported by independent outcomes
  and disjoint edit ownership, within three sequential cohorts.
- C-03: Harness profiles remain harness-owned. Selected tests are not profile
  verdicts; pending work is not a pass; a gate runs once per authoritative
  attempt, with existing idempotency and entry-gate reuse preserved.
- C-04: Baseline normalization must retain assertion substance, test identity,
  failure multiplicity, command identity, exit code, signal, and timeout changes.
- C-05: A valid recorded snapshot remains authoritative. Invalid snapshots and
  invalid configuration needed to start a new run remain errors. Do not change
  `active_config`, persistent model settings, or snapshots to repair drift.
- C-06: Preserve workspace policies and detection or prevention of actual
  unauthorized writes. A shared checkout delta alone does not identify its
  author. Missing enforcement or custody evidence must be explicit.
- C-07: Retain the 60-second watch cadence, the existing attach and recovery
  rules, and the distinction between a live process, a completed worker, and a
  successful product result.
- C-08: Preserve synchronous delegation mutex ownership, prompt-on-stdin,
  credential isolation, model checks, resume semantics, bounded output, and
  timeout cleanup while adding incremental evidence.
- C-09: Read-only stages receive no shell tool. Execution observations must be
  collected independently through a bounded, declared harness operation before
  the observation is graded. Missing evidence cannot become a pass.

### Out of scope

- OOS-01: Repairs for unselected TRACE findings, general workflow redesign,
  release metadata changes, and retroactive waivers or alterations to incident
  verdicts.
- OOS-02: Token counts, native host UI changes, usage fallbacks, and cost
  investigation. Event transport may carry safe session and tool metadata but
  does not add token accounting or a new dashboard.

### Open questions and dispositions

- Q-01: How can a compliant source worker submit before harness profiles run?
  Resolved: add `pending_harness` only for shell criteria the resolved invocation
  assigns to the harness. Submission runs otherwise eligible checks and resolves
  them through deterministic evidence, retaining the worker's original claim.
  Current evidence: `src/lib/validation/stage-output.ts`,
  `src/lib/engine/submit.ts`, `src/lib/engine/submit-helpers.ts`, and

## Engineering plan

### Architecture

Use existing invocation preparation, executor adapters, evidence workers,
repository-check comparison, submission, and watch. Add only three bounded
mechanisms where current interfaces lack the needed information: a Copilot relay
with a typed live record, process write custody evidence, and a verification
execution collector. No dependency or framework is needed.

1. Gate ownership: introduce `pending_harness` in the shared criterion
   vocabulary, schema, normalization, field contract, and scaffolder. Only
   invocation-resolved harness shell criteria accept it. An untouched scaffold
   still cannot submit. Preflight validates worker-owned claims first. Submission
   resolves pending entries from authoritative deterministic checks before a
   success can be recorded. Preserve the original self-evaluation alongside the
   resolved evidence; never forge a worker pass. A policy-disabled gate has an
   explicit disabled result and authority, not a fabricated execution. Missing,
   skipped-without-authority, or failed required results cannot settle success.
2. Failure comparison: parse recognized TAP/test-runner failure records into
   command, stable case identity, assertion/error substance, and occurrence
   counts. Restrict progress/hash removal to known execution metadata positions.
   Do not erase arbitrary hexadecimal values inside expected/actual assertions.
   Preserve conservative diagnostics for unsupported tools and independent
   failure statuses. Retain readers for recorded raw-output results so replay
   does not require a suite rerun or rewritten baselines.
3. Lifecycle isolation: catch only typed live-configuration/projection
   compatibility errors in advisory reads after a valid recorded snapshot is
   established. Keep unrelated filesystem, snapshot, and program errors visible.
   Make the existing candidate execution route durable and documented: use the
   candidate's `bin/run-built`/CLI, preserve `PANCREATOR_ROOT` and the installation
   working directory, and do not inherit `PANCREATOR_EXEC_ROOT` into unrelated
   child fixtures. A controller compile failure must not prevent an explicitly
   selected healthy candidate from administering the recorded run. Do not
   silently select another build or preserve a stale build as current.
4. Copilot transport: retain `ExternalExecutorAdapter.run` as synchronous. A
   compiled Node relay reads its request on stdin, spawns Copilot asynchronously,
   parses JSONL across arbitrary byte boundaries, and emits sanitized incremental
   evidence while the outer adapter waits for a final machine result. Resolve
   secrets from the child environment; never serialize credentials into the
   relay request, argv, files, or progress records. The relay owns child cleanup.
   Keep final stdout/stderr audit compatibility and do not replay live events a
   second time at completion.
   Reserve relay stdout for the final machine envelope. Forward sanitized live
   progress through inherited stderr into the enclosing wrapper's log and the
   append-only event file before exit. Carry accumulated sanitized CLI
   stdout/stderr in the final envelope for audit compatibility; the parent must
   not replay them as new live progress. This avoids buffering the only visible
   progress channel behind the synchronous parent.
5. Process custody: use existing `stageWriteRoots`, `resolveWriteSandbox`,
   `processStartIdentity`, and wrapper records. Record actual write roots
   separately from CLI read/add-dir roots. Bind each launch to run, invocation,
   role, attempt, executor, PID plus start identity, and enforcement mode.
   Only proven own writes or denied own attempts count against the worker.
   Proven foreign mutations are recorded as external observations. When neither
   enforcement nor sufficient actor evidence exists, record an explicit
   unverified attribution result and remediation; do not silently ignore a
   possible own write or call a shared delta proof of ownership.
6. Process observation: consult the launch/heartbeat record even if a platform
   handle has no agent-index entry. A fresh heartbeat and matching live process
   suppress quiet-fallback, not deterministic faults. Two consecutive wakes for
   the same dead/stopped/stale call retain their named stall cause. Final
   execution evidence wins over heartbeat liveness. Missing result, failed exit,
   timeout, malformed records, PID reuse, or a result emitted before exit cannot
   falsely complete a worker.
7. Read-only verification: prepare output scaffolds idempotently before all
   read-only delegations. Before QA dispatch, collect ratified concrete case
   operations; before final verifier dispatch, collect mandatory named
   reproductions and spot checks. Use structured argv operations rather than
   evaluating free-text case descriptions. Validate identity, workspace, write
   roots, timeout, and authorized operation definitions, and reject profile
   commands in live cases. Requests and manifests live in declared run evidence.
   Reuse current gate evidence for profile verdicts. The harness produces raw
   observations; QA/verifier independently grades them. Missing or new disputed
   operations route to authorized collection/remediation before grading, rather
   than asking a shell-less worker to run them or inventing a pass. Output
   validation remains a harness operation on the final worker output.

   The declaration shape is `data.test_plan[].execution.operations` for ratified
   live cases and `data.verification_execution_operations` for source-authorized
   reproduction handoffs. Each version-1 operation contains `id`, `criterion`
   or `finding`, `argv`, `cwd`, `timeout_ms`, `write_roots`, and
   `evidence_paths`. All paths resolve from the declared workspace or run
   evidence root; they cannot grant writes outside the stage's collector policy.
   Operation declarations are data, not worker tool grants.

   For a dispute discovered after launch, an evidence worker writes the declared
   `<evidence-report>.execution-request.json` sidecar; a stage verifier uses
   `data.verification_execution_requests`. A request contains only operation ids
   and the missing observation, never executable authority. The evidence
   dispatcher collects a newly requested authorized operation and reruns only
   its consuming evidence role against the new manifest. Cache by invocation,
   operation definition, and source fingerprint; archive prior reports and do
   not rerun an unchanged completed request. A final verifier that still lacks
   a required observation returns the existing blocked shape with
   `blocking_reason` and `missing_evidence_paths`, without a product verdict.
   Its non-executing request travels through the existing authorized recovery
   route. New operation definitions come from the plan or source-authorized
   remediation before the next verification visit, not from a read-only worker.
   No new workflow stage, automatic approval, or general execution endpoint is
   introduced.

### Shared handoff interfaces

The stream chunk defines an additive, versioned live-record contract in
`src/lib/executors/delegation-live.ts`. Its state is separate from the immutable
final execution audit. Include run/invocation/role/attempt identifiers, executor,
launch time, relay and child PID/start identities, optional wrapper record path,
optional observed session id, heartbeat timestamp, sequence number, and terminal
exit/error information when known. A valid missing session id means "not yet
observed", not a made-up session. Heartbeat cadence is at most 60 seconds; use
30 seconds by default. The linked wrapper is read using its record and
heartbeat, not a presumed agent-index id. Bound records to their invocation and
reject path escape or stale-attempt reuse.

Incremental events retain source order within each stream, record their stream
and sequence, and distinguish assistant, tool, session, completion, and diagnostic
events. Cross-stream receipt order is recorded rather than presented as a
provider-guaranteed ordering. Redaction happens before persistence or display,
including secrets split across chunks; stdin prompts are never echoed. A final
`result` event and process exit are separate observations.

The scope chunk extends that contract's custody metadata additively; it does not
change event sequencing or heartbeat semantics. The watch chunk consumes it and
does not edit executor transport. The verification chunk consumes the gate
ownership contract and does not grant tools by editing executor adapters.

Verification collection uses a separate versioned manifest with operation id,
case/criterion or finding id, run/invocation/attempt, argv, workspace-relative cwd,
allowed scratch/output paths, timeout, start/end, exit/signal, sanitized raw
evidence paths, and source fingerprint. Accept only operations ratified in a
plan or supplied by an already source-authorized reproduction path and listed on
the invocation. A read-only worker's request may select a declared operation;
it cannot authorize arbitrary commands. A missing definition routes to an
explicit evidence gap for authorized collection. Execution failure is evidence,
not necessarily a collector infrastructure failure.

### Dependencies and migration

No new packages. Keep old final delegation records and raw repository-check
results readable. Older invocations without live records retain the existing
explicit fallback; lack of a new record is never proof of liveness. Previously
accepted worker pass/fail outputs stay valid. `unevaluated` remains an unfinished
scaffold value. New pending results are interpreted only under the resolved
invocation's harness ownership. Do not edit old snapshots to adopt a new
contract.

Free-text historical live cases do not become executable shell strings. When
mandatory collection lacks structured operations, report the missing operation
and its authorized author instead of attempting an implicit translation.
Keep direct collection artifacts separate from QA judgments and profile gates.

Every child updates its relevant tests, authored documentation, and module
index through existing repository tooling. Avoid manual changes to generated
indexes. Shared aggregate index generation must be serialized with cohort
integration; it is bookkeeping, not another delivery outcome. Source code and
policy changes remain subject to a later proper release before landing.

declared impacted checks and their named new tests. The harness owns required

spend another profile execution to manufacture worker evidence. Do not run the
